title: Facilitate without turning discovery into a pitch
nav: 1. Facilitate without turning discovery into a pitch
objective: Respond to a participant who interrupts every workflow discussion with a feature request.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: Good facilitation gives the conversation a clear structure and then lets the customer do most of the talking.
Glean's Visioning playbook asks for an open, consultative, and strategic tone, and warns against checklist-style or interrogative discovery. In practice:

items: **Open** by stating the purpose, the agenda, the decision you need, and the time.
**Assign roles:** a facilitator, a note-taker, a timekeeper, and a technical owner for capability questions.
**Use open questions** and play back what you heard so it can be corrected.
**Make the work visible:** effort-and-impact tables, a whiteboard, and sample scenarios.

blocks.x: Ask the question, then let the customer answer it. Paraphrase what they said instead of reframing it into a product requirement. Don't treat silence or politeness as agreement.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: Don't commit to features, timelines, or roadmap items during a workshop. Capture capability questions for the right technical owner.
Neutral facilitation protects the evidence. Leading questions get you agreement, not information.

blocks.title: Leading versus open questions
blocks.alt: A comparison of leading questions with open alternatives. For example, asking whether Glean agents would make the process faster becomes asking what slows the process down today.

items.b: What slows this process down today?

items.a: This is your biggest problem, right?
items.b: Which problem costs the most, and why?
When did this last happen, and what did you do?
